stem: A team is deciding between DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Amazon ElastiCache for two caching needs: one workload reads from a DynamoDB table with a small set of extremely popular keys, and the other reads from an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database with a similarly skewed read pattern. Which TWO pairings correctly match a caching service to its workload? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: ElastiCache for the RDS PostgreSQL workload
DAX for the RDS PostgreSQL workload
ElastiCache exclusively for the DynamoDB workload, in place of DAX
Amazon Redshift as the cache layer for both workloads

rationale: DAX is purpose-built to sit in front of DynamoDB and fits a DynamoDB table with a small set of hot keys, while ElastiCache sits in front of a relational database like RDS PostgreSQL and fits its skewed read pattern instead. DAX only works in front of DynamoDB, so pairing it with an RDS PostgreSQL database is not a supported combination. ElastiCache can technically cache anything, but choosing it over DAX for the DynamoDB workload gives up DAX's transparent, no-code-change fit for that exact case. Redshift is an analytical data warehouse, not a caching service, for either workload.
